title: Soft-reserve regional affinity with graceful model-demotion fallback
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: When dedicated pools saturate, current spillover to hosted endpoints can lead to unexpected latency spikes and model-quality regressions for high-priority tenants. Goal: Implement a soft-reserve regional affinity policy that preserves tenant performance while enabling controlled hosted spillover with ordered model-demotion (variant fallback) and automated safeguards (circuit breakers, decay, and tenant preemption).
acceptance_criteria: Router can allocate soft-reservations per tenant/region (configurable % of dedicated pool) and fall back to hosted per policy
Policy supports ordered model-variant demotion list (e.g., model-v1 -> model-v1-quantized -> model-v0-small) with SLO-aware selection
Circuit-breaker triggers prevent >5% p99 latency deviation for reserved tenants during spillover
End-to-end integration tests and a staged canary show no more than 2% increase in overall 95th latency across synthetic workload
Operational dashboards (per-tenant latency, spillover rate, model-demote events) created and wired to alerting
notes: 2026-03-02: Spike complete — implemented prototype soft-reserve bookkeeping using token-bucket counters sharded by tenant-region. Patch adds per-tenant 'soft_quota' and a decay window of 30m.

2026-03-04: Perf test in staging (50 tenants, realistic seq dist) — dedicated occupancy improved by 12% for top-tier tenants; overall p99 increased by ~3% under synthetic burst. Observed pressure points in queue sizing when many tenants hit soft-reserve simultaneously.

2026-03-06: Design review with PM and SRE. Decided on multi-phase rollout: 1) enable soft-reserve accounting (read-only dashboards), 2) enable policy enforcement with conservative thresholds (+20% headroom), 3) enable model-demotion ordering and resident circuit-breakers.

2026-03-08: Edge-case: cross-region preference where tenant pins region A but backend has spare capacity in region B. Agreed to prefer regional affinity unless latency penalty <20ms and tenant allows region fallback via opt-in flag.
2026-03-09: Review feedback from Design: UI should surface 'current effective model variant' and 'demotion history' to aid debugging. Add API fields to response metadata for observability.
2026-03-11: SRE suggested throttling ramp for host-side spillover at 1% increments per minute for top-tier tenants to avoid cascade; accepted and added to route-enforcer.
2026-03-12: Preparing PR for canary. TODO: add integration test for variant ordering under KV-cache warm vs cold scenarios.
technical_decisions: Soft-reserve semantics: reservation is a moving-window budget (token-bucket) that allows temporary oversubscription but enforces long-term fairness via decay and hard-preempt if sustained over threshold
Spillover ordering: prefer same-architecture model variants (fp16 -> int8 -> quantized) to reduce quality delta; for architecture-incompatible fallbacks use structured response validation
Circuit-breaker: trip when p99 latency for reserved tenant > SLO * 1.25 over a 5-minute window or when error rate > 1% absolute increase

Routing heuristic: combine (1) tenant tier weight, (2) region affinity score, (3) pool spare capacity estimate, and (4) model quality delta penalty into a single cost function — thresholded to decide allocation
Tenant preemption: during critical shortages, allow voluntary preemption of burst tokens from P2/P3 tenants but never forcibly demote P0 tenants without explicit consent flag
open_risks: Quality regressions if quantized variants are served for synchronous production workloads; need to tie into existing eval suite before wide rollout
Billing complexity: routed requests across dedicated and hosted may require clearer attribution for reserved capacity billing and credits
Operator complexity: more moving parts increase alert fatigue; must consolidate alerts and provide single-pane-of-glass runbook
implementation_plan: Phase 0: telemetry-only rollout (dashboard shows soft-reserves + simulated spillover decisions) — 1 week
Phase 1: enforcement behind feature-flag with conservative thresholds + canary tenants (5 tenants) — 2 weeks
Phase 2: open enforcement to all tenants with auto-fallback and circuit-breakers enabled — 1 week
Phase 3: monitor and tune thresholds; add tenant-configurable options (region-fallback opt-in, demotion blacklist) — ongoing
remediation_plan: If rollout causes regressions: immediate rollback to feature-flag off, run automated corrective scripts to move affected tenants back to dedicated pools, and open a post-mortem linking to incident dashboard and remedial PRs.
